items.t: Led a bipartisan coalition against a spring 2018 ballot measure that would have eliminated the treasurer's office, which voters rejected (2018).
items.q: Godlewski led a bipartisan coalition that worked against a measure on the ballot that spring that would have eliminated the treasurer’s office. Voters rejected it

items.t: Says she is committed to transforming the Secretary of State's office to deliver accessible services, expand economic opportunities and strengthen the state's democracy.
items.q: As the 29th Secretary of State, Sarah is committed to transforming the office to best serve the people of Wisconsin by delivering quality, accessible services, expanding economic opportunities, and further strengthening the state’s democracy.

record.t: Was appointed Secretary of State by Gov. Tony Evers on March 17, the day the previous secretary resigned.
record.q: Democratic Gov. Tony Evers tapped Godlewski for the role on March 17, the day her predecessor, longtime Secretary of State Doug La Follette, abruptly resigned less than three months into his eleventh consecutive term.

record.t: Served as state treasurer before becoming Secretary of State and ran unsuccessfully for U.S. Senate in 2022.
record.q: Godlewski, who previously served as state treasurer, was coming off an unsuccessful 2022 midterm bid for U.S. Senate.

record.t: Was appointed Wisconsin Secretary of State by Gov. Tony Evers, who chose to appoint her rather than call a special election.
record.q: The governor said he appointed Sarah Godlewski to the position rather than call a special election.

record.t: Announced a $73.5 million Common School Fund distribution, described in the release as the largest in the Fund's history, at a press conference in Eau Claire.
record.q: Wisconsin Secretary of State Sarah Godlewski today announced a record-breaking $73.5 million distribution from the Common School Fund, the largest in the Fund’s history, during a press conference held at the Memorial High School Library in Eau Claire.
